olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove that for every positive integer $n$, there exists an $n$-digit number divisible by $5^n$ all of whose digits are odd.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A convex polygon $P$ is dissected into smaller convex polygons by all its diagonals. All sides and diagonals of $P$ have rational lengths. Prove all sides of all polygons in the dissection are rational.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: For any sequence $A=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $0\leq a_i\leq i$, define $t(A)$ by $t(a_i)=$ number of terms before $a_i$ that differ from $a_i$. Show fewer than $n$ applications of $t$ lead to a fixed sequence $B$ with $t(B)=B$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circle through $A,B$ meets segments $AC,BC$ at $D,E$. Lines $AB,DE$ meet at $F$; lines $BD,CF$ meet at $M$. Prove $MF=MC$ iff $MB\cdot MD=MC^2$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003

source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: At vertices of a regular hexagon write nonneg­ative integers summing to $2003^{2003}$. Bert may replace any vertex value by the absolute difference of its two neighbors. Prove Bert can make all values 0.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2003
